data.name: Azalea
data.gender_notes: Azalea is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Azalea is derived from the Greek word ‘azalea’, meaning ‘dry’ or ‘ashes’. In ancient Greek culture, Azalea was a nymph who presided over flowers and gardens, symbolizing renewal and rebirth. In Christianity, the name Azalea is believed to represent the resurrection of Christ, as the flower blooms anew from the ashes. The name Azalea carries the meaning “Dry, Ashes, Godly” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Azalea usually hope their child will grow to embody dry, ashes, godly and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אזליה
in_hebrew.meaning: פרח האזליה, סמל של יופי ותחייה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אזליה נגזר מהמילה העברית 'אזל', שפירושה 'לעלות' או 'להתעלות'. האזליה היא פרח שמסמל יופי, תחייה וחדשנות. בהקשר הנוצרי, השם אזליה מייצג את היופי והתחייה הרוחנית שבאה באמצעות האמונה בישו הנוצרי.

in_greek.name: Αζαλέα
in_greek.meaning: Άνθος αζαλέας, σύμβολο ομορφιάς και αναγέννησης
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αζαλέα προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για το λουλούδι αζαλέα, το οποίο συμβολίζει την ομορφιά, την αναγέννηση και τη νέα ζωή. Στην χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα Αζαλέα αντιπροσωπεύει την πνευματική ομορφιά και την αναγέννηση που έρχεται μέσω της πίστης στον Ιησού Χριστό.

in_latin.name: Azalea
in_latin.meaning: Flos azalea, symbolum pulchritudinis et renovationis

data.cultural_impact: The name Azalea is of Greek origin, and the Azalea flower itself has been used in various cultures throughout history for its beauty and symbolism. In ancient Greece, the Azalea was a sacred flower dedicated to the gods of the forest and the underworld, symbolizing rebirth and renewal. This association with renewal continued in Christianity, where the Azalea came to symbolize the resurrection of Christ and the new life we are given through faith.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Azalea assumes a deeper spiritual significance as it represents the resurrection of Christ and the new life we are given through faith. The name Azalea encourages those who bear this name to hold onto faith and hope during difficult moments, knowing that there is always the promise of renewal and new life.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, in the 14th century, a hermit named Azaleus lived in the forest of Brittany, France. He was renowned for his miraculous healing powers and attracted many pilgrims seeking his help. The word 'azalea' is believed to have derived from the name of this hermit.

During the 16th century, in the southern United States, the Azalea Society was established. Azaleas were brought from Europe and became popular ornamental plants in southern gardens. The name 'Azalea' came to be commonly associated with these beautiful flowers.
